area: WP 7.1 (citations rewritten) and the code and test budget picture
summary: WP 7.1 as written (V3_MILESTONES.md:756; V3_INSTRUCTION_ARCHITECTURE.md:1526-1533) rewrites citations in v2's skills and agents. Those 79 files sit under archive/v2/ssdt-agent/{skills,agents} and the archive cannot be edited (DECISIONS.md:13). knowledge/ does not exist yet (Citations.cs:44 excuses knowledge/ paths until M7). v3's own tool documents (Documents.cs:135) already cite ledgers by dbchange/ledgers/ and carry no v2 citation form. So the rewrite has no target until WP 7.2 moves the files. What 7.1 can land now is the citation test's form rules, which every file 7.2 moves must then pass, plus value O3's test (VALUES.md:74 names it as WP 7.1's), which today fails only at VALUES.md:51. The budget, counted the way Budgets.cs counts it: kernel 2,365/6,800, io 5,203/6,400, cli 1,289/1,700, tests 15,102/20,000, golden 1,461/3,000; io grew from 2,213 to 5,203 after the 2026-09-24 ruling commit 1922566 with no new milestone, and ran 2.81 times its M0+M1 plan. I measured a reflow to 140 characters: it joins almost nothing (io 20-52 lines, cli 6-10) and splits a lot (io 710 lines and cli 181 lines are over 140 now). It raises io to 5,589-5,755 and cli to 1,409-1,448, so reflowing cannot defend the ceilings, and io is the first ceiling hit: in M2 (WP 2.5, or WP 2.3 at M1's overrun ratio) once the work that needs no person lands first.

items.remaining: In tests/Budgets.Tests/Citations.cs: (1) Add a private static Forms table of (Regex Pattern, string What, string Instead). It holds four rules. The finding-by-file rule matches `(?<!archive/v2/ssdt-agent/)\bFINDINGS_AND_CHANGES\.md`; instead, cite the finding by its identifier, F<n>. The sample-by-v2-path rule matches `(?<![\w/])(?:\.\./)*sample-prs/`; instead, cite knowledge/samples/<shape>.md. The handbook-by-number rule matches `handbook(?:'s)?\s+(?:file\s+)?\**\d+|\(=\s*§\d+|(?<![\w/])\d{2}-[A-Z][\w-]+\.md`; instead, cite the chapter by its title. The ledger-by-v2-or-bare-path rule matches `(?<![\w/.-])(?:(?:\.\./)*(?:ssdt-agent/)?estate/|ledgers/)?(?:in-flight|operations|refusals|reviewers|row-tiers|scale-datapoints|toolchain|cdc-tracked)\.md`; instead, cite knowledge/ledgers/<name> for the template the tool seeds or dbchange/ledgers/<name> for the SSDT repository's rows. A match inside a backticked span that starts with archive/ is provenance and passes. (2) Add Theory Every_document_of_the_repository_cites_a_finding_by_identifier_a_sample_by_shape_the_handbook_by_title_and_a_ledger_by_its_path(string document), Category fast, MemberData ToolDocuments. It runs Forms over each Documents.Blocks(document) text and fails with '<doc>:<line>: '<match>' cites <What>; <Instead>'. (3) Add a findings set: the '## ~*F(\d+) ·' headings of knowledge/findings.md when Repository.Contains it; otherwise the '^- \*\*F(\d+) —' items of archive/v2/ssdt-agent/FINDINGS_AND_CHANGES.md. Every `\bF\d+\b` in a tool document must name one; VALUES.md row ids use no F, so there is no collision. (4) For documents under knowledge/ only (none yet), every backticked `dbchange <word>` must name a Contract.Verbs row, built or not. (5) Extend the class summary to say what each form rule enforces. Optional: hold the twelve shape names of §7.8 as data. Leave this out unless WP 7.2 fixes the split-table phase file names; once knowledge/samples/ exists, path resolution already catches a wrong name.

items.name: The reflow to 140-character lines, measured (DECISIONS.md:55)
items.evidence:
.editorconfig sets no max_line_length (only charset, end_of_line, indent, braces, file-scoped namespaces), and no test checks line width.
Lines over 140 characters today: kernel 160 (54 comments), io 710 (220 comments), cli 181 (47), tests 1,377 (293). The longest are io/Git.cs at 302 and cli/Contract.cs at 423. The worst files: io/SqlServer.cs 148 over, io/Ssdt.cs 131, io/Git.cs 76, cli/Contract.cs 46, cli/Render.cs 39.
The estimator, kept in the scratch folder and run read-only, groups code into statements by their indent and re-wraps them greedily at 140 (continuations at indent+4, breaking only at spaces outside string literals), and word-wraps comment paragraphs; raw strings are frozen. Three models:
(a) Efficient: every statement and paragraph repacked. kernel 2,401, io 5,589, cli 1,409, tests 16,051. Joins save io 52 (47 code, 5 comment) and cli 10; splits add io 438 and cli 130.
(b) House style, the realistic one: only statements and comments holding a line over 140 are re-wrapped, and an overlong one-line summary becomes the tag, its text and the closing tag. kernel 2,497, io 5,755 (+552: joins 20, splits 572), cli 1,448 (+159), tests 16,415.
(c) Split-only upper bound: kernel 2,529, io 5,931, cli 1,486, tests 16,536.
Cross-check: CSharpier 1.3.0 with printWidth 140 gives kernel 2,796, io 7,650, cli 2,122. At printWidth 1000 it gives 2,235, 5,024 and 1,449, so that style itself costs little and the growth at 140 is wrapping.
Per file, house style: io/SqlServer.cs 997 to 1,111; io/Ssdt.cs 767 to 848; io/Git.cs 405 to 476; cli/Render.cs 407 to 439; cli/Contract.cs 283 to 327. Test files that would pass 800: ModelElementsTests 1,077, ContractTests 865, Register/ErrorPaths 842, TargetTests 835, GitTests 808.

items.remaining: Which work package crosses first: io's ceiling. At plan figures, M2's last io package, WP 2.5 (io/Predict and the verbs predict, classify and check cdc, after 2.2 and 2.3), crosses unless every io package lands at or under its estimate. Under a 140-character rule it crosses even then (6,445). At M1's measured io overrun (2.81 times), M2's io alone is about 1,940 lines, more than the 1,197 of headroom, and WP 2.3 (io/AggregateQueries) crosses. Next come tests (M3), cli (M3 if reflowed, M4 otherwise) and the code total (M5). The first package over makes its own pull request red, in Budgets.Each_budget_holds_its_ceiling("io") and later The_code_together_holds_its_ceiling, unless a DECISIONS.md line raises the ceiling in the same pull request. The operator's options: (1) raise the ceilings to fit the plan; at plan figures that is at least io 8,900 (9,400 at 140 characters), cli 2,200 (2,350), code 16,600 (17,400) and tests 27,300 (28,600), and M1 overran its plan two to three times; (2) hold them and order a compaction of io, or a move of its pure logic into the kernel, which has 1,225 lines spare after its plan; candidates are SqlServer.cs (997 against 700 planned), Ssdt.cs (767 against 400) and the 1,943 lines in io files the plan never named; (3) cut or defer planned io, such as M7's Knowledge.cs (400) or M6's Ossys.cs (370). Separately: if 140 characters is meant to be a rule, it needs a test (a fast Budgets test over kernel/, io/, cli/ and tests/, not today's golden corpus) and a reflow pass that costs the numbers above.
